name: Mount Eerie
label: P.W. Elverum & Sun
lede: Phil Elverum shut down the Microphones in 2003, took the name of the mountain above his hometown and has released almost everything since on a label he runs himself. After his wife Geneviève Castrée died in 2016, the albums he made about it became the best-known of his career.

eras.title: A kid from Anacortes finds a four-track
eras.text: Phil Elverum grows up in Anacortes, Washington, under the mountain he will later name a project after. A record-store job, an invitation from Beat Happening's Bret Lunsford to drum in D+, and a move to Olympia put him in the middle of the K Records world.

years.src: Wikipedia: Phil Elverum · Wikipedia: Mount Eerie
years.h: Phil Whitman Elverum is born in Anacortes, under the mountain
years.p: He starts on tuba, switches to drums at fourteen and forms a band called Nubert Circus. His father made mixtapes for him and his sister.
years.xp:
Wikipedia has him born May 26, 1978, in the town his whole catalog keeps returning to: the mountain, the ferry, the woods. The name Mount Eerie comes from Mount Erie, which looms over Anacortes.

Until 2003 he spelled his surname Elvrum. This page uses Elverum throughout.

years.h: Love Tara by [[Eric's Trip|fe6365d4-74f3-4706-9aea-d061a394722d]] shows him what a record can sound like
years.p: A promo cassette of the Moncton band's homemade album reached Elverum through his record-store job. A dog barking and a car passing in the background "blew my mind," he told Exclaim!.
years.xp:
What got him, he said, was that "it felt homemade." The four-track, tactile feel of Rick White's recordings has kept shaping how he works.

He made a pilgrimage to Moncton in the late 1990s and later made two records with Eric's Trip's [[Julie Doiron|44727d86-a37c-449f-aa91-4a8554127336]].

years.src: Wikipedia: Phil Elverum · Wikipedia: The Microphones
years.h: Beat Happening's Bret Lunsford recruits him for D+
years.p: Elverum met Lunsford while working at The Business, a record store in Anacortes. Lunsford brought him into D+ alongside [[Karl Blau|688d2d9d-8f49-4187-b558-2c961c699ab1]], and the same year Elverum began recording as [[The Microphones|6f2f87e7-3ce9-4f1c-81dd-6f068a78cf26]].
years.xp: Wikipedia puts both the D+ recruitment and the founding of the Microphones around 1996, the Microphones starting on cassettes for the KNW-YR-OWN label. The first full albums came later: Tests (Elsinor, 1998), then Don't Wake Me Up and It Was Hot, We Stayed in the Water on K Records.

years.h: Elverum moves to Olympia and records at Dub Narcotic Studio
years.p: He lived in Olympia until 2002, working at a food co-op and recording in [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]]'s studio. By 2000 he was living at the Track House, a hub for local musicians.

eras.title: Olympia, a record people keep returning to, then a new name
eras.text: In Olympia, Elverum records The Glow Pt. 2, the album that makes the Microphones a name. Then he closes the band with a five-track album named for his hometown mountain, and changes the project's name to match.

years.cap: The Glow Pt. 2 (2001), cover art from a 1933-34 Dutch cookbook.
years.h: The Microphones release The Glow Pt. 2
years.p: Elverum recorded it at Dub Narcotic from May 2000 to March 2001 on 16-track tape, and K Records put it out. Pitchfork named it the best album of 2001.
years.xp:
Elverum played and produced nearly everything. [[Mirah|e4c226f2-ba57-483f-be6b-3391112244b8]] often came to the early-morning sessions and encouraged him, and [[Khaela Maricich|07d0cdc9-6e87-4645-ba65-a042961c6e7c]], who engineered, turns up in the songs. The cover art comes from a Dutch cookbook of 1933-34.

Pitchfork first scored it 9.2, later revised to 9.3. Elverum himself has called the idea of albums being "essential" a "total myth." [[Lil Peep|92da4329-77a4-425c-8e92-4280110cace9]] later sampled it.

yt: The Microphones play "Great Ghosts" live in Japan, February 19, 2003
years.h: The last Microphones album takes its name from the mountain
years.p: Five tracks and 40:51 follow a life from womb to death, sung by different voices as different characters. Recorded at Dub Narcotic from November 2001 to June 2002; Pitchfork gave it 8.9.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mount Eerie · Wikipedia: Mount Eerie (album)
years.h: "Mount Eerie is a new project. The Microphones was completed"
years.p: Elverum announced the change in September 2003, moved home to Anacortes and started spelling his surname Elverum.
years.xp: He explained the name in a 2014 interview as a way of tying the music to its place. The album and the project both borrow the mountain's name. His subjects, per Wikipedia, moved from recording equipment to stranger, darker, natural ones.

eras.title: Back home, with a label of his own
eras.text: In Anacortes, Elverum builds the machinery he still runs himself: his own label, his own packaging, a marriage and a run of records that go from fold-out sleeves to a black metal detour.

years.cap: Elverum with Castrée, performing as Woelv, at the Gob Gob show in Denver
years.src: Wikipedia: Phil Elverum · Wikipedia: Geneviève Castrée
years.h: Elverum and Geneviève Castrée marry on a leap day
years.p: They had met in 2003 through mutual friends and settled in Anacortes, where they became central to the local scene, including the What The Heck festival.
years.xp: Castrée was born April 9, 1981, in Loretteville, Quebec, and began as a teenager making minicomics. Her first book, Lait Frappé, came out in 2000. She made music under two names: Woelv (2006-2007) and Ô Paon (2009-2015).

years.src: Wikipedia: Mount Eerie · Wikipedia: Phil Elverum
yt: Full set, Pacific Cultural Center, Santa Cruz, May 26, 2004
years.h: Elverum founds P.W. Elverum & Sun, Ltd.
years.p: The label would release nearly all Mount Eerie records. He prints, packs and ships the vinyl and merch himself.
years.xp: The same year brought Seven New Songs of "Mount Eerie", Mount Eerie Dances with Wolves (a 12" recorded live to acetate on an Australian tour) and the live triple album Live in Copenhagen.

years.h: Mount Eerie's first studio album comes with footnotes
years.p: "No Flashlight": Songs of the Fulfilled Night arrived in a fold-out sleeve, an early sign of how much he treats the object as part of the record.

years.h: A winter alone in a Norwegian cabin becomes a 144-page book
years.p: Elverum wrote the songs for Dawn in winter 2002-03 after a breakup, in a remote cabin in Norway. The CD came bound into a hardcover with his journal entries and drawings.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, Dawn is the third Mount Eerie full-length, catalog number ELV 017, with [[Karl Blau|688d2d9d-8f49-4187-b558-2c961c699ab1]] engineering. AllMusic, Tiny Mix Tapes and Sputnikmusic each gave it three stars out of five.

q: It's definitely not a black metal album.
years.h: Wind's Poem gets called a black metal album. Elverum disagrees
years.p: That was Elverum's verdict, as he told an interviewer, on making a "kitschy genre album." He recorded it with [[Nicholas Krgovich|1a90d42f-a474-4904-835b-b2414f89d36c]] in Anacortes, and Pitchfork gave it 8.2.
years.xp:
Sessions ran from February 14, 2008 to March 27, 2009 at Nowhere in Anacortes. He cites Xasthur's Subliminal Genocide and Burzum among the sources of the sound, but rejects the label outright.

On tour he played with Krgovich, [[Tara Jane O'Neil|a9a6334c-1541-4aef-8092-fe743f0df64f]] and Julia Jacklin. One reviewer said the shows delivered distortion "so heavy the walls shook."

eras.title: Fog and a church studio
eras.text: Elverum makes his most atmospheric records at a studio in Anacortes, releases two companion albums in one year and is invited to play for an old hero.

years.h: Clear Moon trades distortion for ominous rumbling
years.p: Recorded over fifteen months at the Unknown, a studio in Anacortes. Where Wind's Poem roared, this one lets feedback squalls through in isolation. Pitchfork gave it 8.3.
years.xp: Recording ran October 3, 2010 to January 7, 2012. Elverum chose not to release it as a double album with its companion, feeling that would overwhelm listeners.

years.h: Ocean Roar arrives as the foggy twin of Clear Moon
years.p: Elverum called it the opposite of its sibling: a wall of blue-grey fog and a half-remembered drive to the winter ocean at night. Pitchfork gave it 8.1.
years.xp: The album runs 38:43 and includes a cover of Popol Vuh's "Engel Der Luft." In October 2012 a 7-inch paired condensed versions of both records, with side B playing every Ocean Roar track at once.

years.cap: Elverum as Mount Eerie, on a bill with Earth and O Paon, 2012
years.h: Jeff Mangum picks Mount Eerie for All Tomorrow's Parties
years.p: Elverum played the ATP that Mangum curated at Minehead, England, and called it an honor to be chosen. [[Neutral Milk Hotel|a506f761-2c22-4b2f-8a94-bd748c2c8f75]] was a band he loved.

years.h: A converted church in Anacortes is the studio for Sauna
years.p: Recorded June 2013 to August 2014 at the Unknown. Pitchfork gave it 8.1, and Metacritic scored it 82.
years.xp: Elverum called it music meant to weigh heavy "like a lot of cold water at night," with the sauna as a place where flames, steam and dim light wipe out ordinary sensation. Some reviewers found the lyrics too literal.

years.src: Wikipedia: Phil Elverum · Wikipedia: Geneviève Castrée
years.h: Castrée is diagnosed with pancreatic cancer
years.p: Their daughter had been born about four months earlier. The cancer was inoperable.

eras.title: After Castrée
eras.text: After Castrée's death, Elverum makes plain-spoken albums at home in Anacortes. They become the best-known records of his career, and he takes them on the road in churches and small halls.

years.h: Geneviève Castrée dies at home in Anacortes, aged 35
years.p: She died of pancreatic cancer on July 9, 2016. Besides her books as a cartoonist, she made music as Woelv and Ô Paon.
years.xp:
Elverum has said she "died at home with me and her parents holding her."

Her graphic novel Susceptible came out in 2012. Drawn & Quarterly published A Bubble (2017) and Maman Apprivoisée (2018) after her death.

years.cap: A Crow Looked at Me (2017), cover photo of Castrée's art studio.
years.src: Wikipedia: A Crow Looked at Me · Wikipedia: Geneviève Castrée
years.h: Elverum records A Crow Looked at Me at home in Anacortes
years.p: He made it from August 31 to December 6, 2016, with a single microphone, an acoustic guitar and some of Castrée's instruments. Pitchfork gave it 9.0.
years.xp:
The cover shows Castrée's former studio, with Elverum's hand holding Joanne Kyger's poem "Night Palace," which mattered to her. The singles "Real Death" (January) and "Ravens" (February 15) came first. Elverum called the album "barely music," and has said he doesn't see it as a tribute.

It came out March 24, 2017. Metacritic scored it 93, Tiny Mix Tapes put it at No. 1 on its year-end list, and it is his best-selling record.

He toured North America in April and September 2017 and Europe that November, often in churches and small halls.

years.h: Pitchfork calls Now Only "part memoir and part magnum opus"
years.p: Elverum recorded the nine songs, averaging seven minutes each, between March 14 and October 9, 2017, in the same room as A Crow Looked at Me. Pitchfork gave it 8.5.
years.xp: Elverum described it as a shift from raw catharsis to looking at how Castrée persists in his life after her death. It carried the singles "Distortion" (January 17) and "Tintin in Tibet" (February 20).

years.h: Elverum marries the actor Michelle Williams
years.p: They wed in the Adirondacks in July 2018 and moved to Brooklyn, separated in January 2019 and were divorced by November 2019. He returned to Washington state.

years.h: (after) is recorded in a Dutch church on November 10, 2017
years.p: Elverum played songs from A Crow Looked at Me and Now Only at the Jacobikerk in Utrecht, during Le Guess Who? Pitchfork gave the live record 8.1.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Nathan Reese wrote that even after so many performances the songs "sound as raw as they did" when first put on paper and tape. Tiny Mix Tapes gave it five out of five.

yt: Tiny Desk concert with Julie Doiron, NPR Music, February 2020
years.h: Elverum and Julie Doiron record Lost Wisdom pt. 2 with the door open
years.p: They made it May 26 to June 1, 2019, and birdsong and jackhammering leak into the tracks. Metacritic scored it 79.
years.xp: Doiron wrote the melodies she sang and Elverum wrote the lyrics. It is a sequel to their 2008 Lost Wisdom.

eras.title: The old name, one more time
eras.text: Elverum revives his old name for a single 44-minute song and a run of shows, then closes it for good with a box set.

years.src: Wikipedia: Microphones in 2020 · Wikipedia: The Microphones
years.h: Elverum revives the Microphones for a single 44-minute song
years.p: Microphones in 2020 runs 44:44. Recorded between May 2019 and May 2020, it came out on P.W. Elverum & Sun under the old name. Pitchfork gave it 8.5 and Best New Music.
years.xp:
Elverum worked the lyrics out by walking around and mumbling them, then wrote them on a nine-foot scroll before recording. The cover is a 1999 photo by [[Mirah|e4c226f2-ba57-483f-be6b-3391112244b8]]. It looks back at The Glow Pt. 2.

The revival began with a one-off Anacortes concert in June 2019.

years.h: Elverum announces the box set Completely Everything, 1996–2021
years.p: It was billed as the final Microphones retrospective. Limited tour dates in 2021 and 2022 preceded the project's end.

eras.title: Night Palace
eras.text: After five years with no Mount Eerie album, Elverum delivers a 26-song double record from his home studio, pitched as a spiritual successor to The Glow Pt. 2.

years.h: Night Palace is announced with "I Walk" and "Broom of Wind"
years.p: Stereogum reported the 26-track album as Mount Eerie's first in five years. Indigo Free directed the video for "Broom of Wind."

years.cap: Elverum solo at Walt Disney Concert Hall, Los Angeles, opening for Dirty Projectors with the LA Phil, c. 2024
years.h: Night Palace is Mount Eerie's first double album
years.p: 26 songs, 80 minutes 47 seconds, recorded between 2022 and 2024 and released on P.W. Elverum & Sun. Elverum works from a home studio on Orcas Island, a ferry ride from Anacortes.
years.xp: The title comes from Joanne Kyger's poem, which appeared on the cover of A Crow Looked at Me. Elverum told Exclaim! the record is edited down from far more recordings, and that an 80-minute album of one mood "would suck."

years.h: Elverum pitches Night Palace as a sequel to The Glow Pt. 2
years.p: His own summary of the album, per Stereogum: meditation, decolonization and backwoods protest songs recorded on reel-to-reel.

q: Feels like a culmination of his work over the past 25 years.
years.src: Wikipedia: Night Palace · Album of the Year
years.h: Night Palace ends 2024 at No. 7 on Pitchfork's list
years.p: Pitchfork's Daniel Bromfield, who gave it 8.3, wrote that it feels like a culmination of Elverum's work over 25 years. The Atlantic put it at No. 1.
years.xp:
Metacritic collected 14 scores for an 86 ("universal acclaim"). Stereogum also ranked it No. 7. Dissent: Slant gave it 60, Paste 75 and Rolling Stone 80, according to Album of the Year.

AllMusic's Heather Phares said it "holds a special place in his discography."

years.h: Warsaw in Brooklyn, then the Bellwether in Los Angeles
years.p: Elverum played Warsaw on November 19 and the Bellwether on November 21 to mark the release.
